calls.title: The noncredit subject title list
calls.text: The list holds 129 headings from the four large noncredit programs as 114 titles. Sam settles which headings join one title, and whether Citizenship, Health and Safety, substantial disabilities and Workforce Preparation take a common code or none.
calls.if_no_reply: The noncredit hold stands and the list stays a draft.

answer.words: "Looks good. Based on a quick check on my phone. Can we go with it and I can look more closely tomorrow and reverse or change anything that looks wrong?" (in session, about 03:50Z). The 114 titles stand and the hold is lifted (#3667); the five categories with no common code keep none (r-noncredit-title-list-go-sam-2026-11-22). He may change the list after a closer look.

calls.title: Aligning 192 Cerritos courses whose M-ID sits under another Common SUBJ
calls.text: Sam's saved subject decisions put 192 Cerritos courses under a Common SUBJ other than the one their M-ID was minted under; ATH's 84 sit under ATHL against his KINE, and on ordinary titles the decided code and the M-ID agree for 253 of 440. Aligning them is a re-mint under the re-mint playbook, with its dry run and alias map.
calls.if_no_reply: Nothing is re-minted; the courses keep their M-IDs and the page shows the decided code beside them.

calls.title: Two forestry courses still sit on AGRI under a parent on ENVR
calls.text: Open Asks Sheet 105 card 1: AGRI M10SY Forest Surveying and AGRI M1104 Introduction to Forest Operations are merged into Forest Ecology, which moved to ENVR on Sheet 104. The dry run that moves both to ENVR is committed; the session's permission check held its apply.
calls.no_reply: Both stay on AGRI, merged into an ENVR parent; nothing else waits on the card.

answer.words: move-both (Open Asks Sheet 107 card 1; applied by S436, kb/forestry_wine_remint_out/2026-10-20-stragglers/)

calls.title: Six curated anchor entries the re-key dry run cannot settle
calls.text: Three collide with other courses on their new Common SUBJ and need fresh numbers; three hospitality entries have no MQ discipline. On no reply they stay unapplied.

next_step.title: The statewide default for a code by the DR-25 route
next_step.text: One Save now settles a code's common subject code at every college using it, on each college's credit form. Next is the statewide default in the subject map for a code that reads the same everywhere, then the per-course reader for noncredit saves and the 8 catalog pages a web search found.

changes.text: Settle a code at every college: one common subject code and one Save write a kb_curation row per college at its credit form's key, under the reviewer's own email; a college a person or filing settled keeps it, a noncredit-only code keeps its category forms (#3687).

Edit on every code row and the course panel over every Subjects surface; every count opens the rows it counts; the surfaces take the window's width; Local titles reads 88 of 101 codes at Los Angeles Pierce

Noncredit codes get a save per COCI noncredit category, keyed SUBJ:college|code|nc:category; 275 codes get a noncredit form, 64 span several categories, 37 have no category on file; a form with no title field writes no title, and a title saved before its category moved shows read-only (#3671).

The daily build reads saved subject decisions: a college's save, then a statewide List filing, then the subject map, then a recommendation; codes with a common code rose from 888 to 918. Shell titles such as work experience stay held, and the mint plan equals main's (#3670).
Santa Ana's and Mt. San Antonio's credit catalogs are filed with their headings; Not read yet fell from 388 to 156 and titled codes rose from 1,412 to 1,636 (#3669).

The noncredit hold is lifted on Sam's word: the noncredit title list no longer reads as a draft, the 54 held rows became ordinary rows, and noncredit and noncredit enhanced courses show apart (#3667).
Sam's 30 Cerritos subject decisions are filed in kb_curation under cohort subjects-s701@bot, with a receipt and a rollback beside it.
Edit and Save on the Subjects page: a signed-in reviewer saves a local title or common code as one kb_curation row, and Take it back removes only that reviewer's own save (#3666).

Three large noncredit catalogs are filed (San Diego College of Continuing Education, Santa Ana School of Continuing Education, Mt. San Antonio noncredit), and a draft noncredit subject title list opens inside Subjects; the list opens on All subjects with a Credit and Noncredit filter, and ATH is KINE (#3662).
A local code opens that college's courses in a side panel, credit and noncredit apart, each with its C-ID, CCN and M-ID (#3661).

The 21 subject pages the catalog indexes link are read and filed (493 courses), and each row with no title shows a recommended local title or common code with its measured level; 108 web searches are filed for the Not in catalog rows (#3660).
The held view, opened from a figure on the Subjects card, lists the local subject codes the pile mint holds on: 1,341 courses, 416 codes, 678 college-and-code pairs.
Both Subjects files rebuild in the daily build when their content changes; a failed step keeps yesterday's file and the publish goes on.

The Subjects card on the Commons front reads 16 colleges, 1,431 college-and-code pairs and 746 printed names; 753 of 1,625 codes get a common subject code from the existing files. Its builder is not in the daily build yet.
Curation step b, the local subject title, has an owner: the Courses bot drafts each title and a curator settles the ones that disagree. Sam left the call to the session on Nov 20.

The anchor re-key applied: 20 curated anchor entries onto their Common SUBJ, 15 keeping their number and 5 on the lowest free number of DIES or PARA; the three hospitality entries stay with the curator (#2938).
The anchor re-key dry run reads the anchor's era from its keys and applies only later maps: 2 re-keys, 15 prefix swaps, 6 for Sam (#2935).
A recorded note settles a weak mnemonic, and the anchor findings are their own re-key item, so nothing waits on a curator (#2857).
Saves read the sign-in at write time, and a lapsed sign-in says so
A row press edits the row and moves the panel; Check alignment audits a typed code
